newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - May 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - May 11.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
SUNDAY TELEGRAPH
-- BARCLAYS OFFERED $750 MILLION FOR FLEET

The multi-millionaire Barclay twins are poised to accept a $750 million offer for the tanker shipping company, Gotaas-Larsen, from a Singaporean business controlled by the son of Indonesia's President Suharto. The sale to Osprey Maritime would be the biggest transaction by the twins.
-- REGAN FORMED BOGUS CO-OP

It has been revealed that Andrew Regan and David Lyons set up a bogus co-op as a front for their failed attempt to take over the Co-operative Wholesale Society (CWS). They formed County Produce as part of a series of intermediaries to hide its true identity and purpose. The company became a corporate member of the CWS and would have been allowed to vote for Regan's bid.
-- GALLAHER FLOATS THIS MONTH

Britain's leading cigarette manufacturer Gallaher Group is set to float on the London stock market at the end of the month at a value of 2.2 billion stg following the publication of its listing particulars. The group will also have an ADR listing in New York to enable US investors to sell out easily.
-- ICI SEEKING NEW POLYESTER PARTNER

ICI is in talks with several of the world's biggest polyester manufacturers, including Hoechst of Germany and America's Dupont and the Dow Chemical Co, in an effort to set up a joint venture that would start the group's planned three billion stg disposal programme.
-- INTERFLORA BRACED FOR BID AFTER FLOWER POWER WAR

America's largest and fastest growing flower delivery business, 1-800 FLOWERS, is set to launch a bid for Interflora. A spokesman for the company said that the UK is at the top of the group's expansion list. The group is interested in the trouble at Interflora which threatens to split the company.
SUNDAY TIMES
-- COMPUTER TIME BOMB 'WILL WRECK BUSINESS'

The Central Computer and Telecommunications Agency, the government arm that handles information technology, is to give business leaders a warning of the dangers faced by industry from the built-in timing fault in computers that threatens chaos at the turn of the century. It has prepared a guide advising how to prepare for the forthcoming "crisis".
-- CITY PUSHES FOR BIG BTR SHAKE-UP

The largest investors in BTR are calling for a radical shake-up after shares tumbled. They would like Ian Strachan, chief executive, to speed up disposals and consider a more radical demerger strategy designed to enhance value, as well as the replacement of its chairman, Elwyn Eilledge.
-- UNILEVER AIMS TO GO DIRECT

The Anglo-Dutch consumer products giant, Unilever, is considering radical diversification into new service-related methods of channelling its foods and personal products to the consumer. The move would be part of a strategy being developed by head of Unilever's UK arm, Niall FitzGerald, and Morris Tabaksblat, his Dutch counterpart, after the sale of Imperial Chemicals Industries, the group's chemicals business.
-- BANK GOVERNOR RULES OUT RAISING BASE RATES

Governor of the Bank of England, Eddie George, has said that the quarter-point rise in base rates to 6.25 percent has put Britain on track to achieve the government's 2.5 percent inflation target. He said that the Bank would not take advantage of its independence to push rates up.
-- CAMELOT MAY GIVE UP RUNNING THE LOTTERY

National Lottery operator Camelot is preparing to give up the running of the lottery in three years if the government carries out its threat to ensure it is non-profit-making. Camelot would have to be completely restructured. Presently it is owned by a consortium, including Cadbury Schweppes, De La Rue, GTech, ICL and Racal.
THE OBSERVER
-- LABOUR TARGETS BT FOR WINDFALL TAX

The paymaster-general of the Labour Party and one of the architects of the windfall tax, Geoffrey Robinson, has said that British Telecom will definitely be hit by the tax in Chancellor Gordon Brown's planned June 10 Budget. BT argued that it should not be included because it is not a monopoly or a utility.
-- EURO MINISTER RED-FACED AS BP ACCUSED OF FLOUTING EU LAW

BP faces legal action for flouting a key European employment law while chaired by the Government's minister for trade in Europe, David Simon. UK and continental unions claim BP broke the law when it set up its European works council without consulting them about its role and make-up, a condition under the Social Chapter.
-- OFTEL RAISES COMPETITION WORRIES OVER BSKYB DIGITAL TV PLANS

BSkyB's bid to win a digital terrestrial television licence is being scrutinised by Oftel, industry regulator, due to the deal's threat to competition. Oftel have submitted a report to the Independent Television Commission, who hand out digital television licenses, which focuses on competition and consumer protection.
-- INDONESIANS FIND BRE-X'S SECRET 'GOLD' LABORATORY

Indonesian sources claim they have found the secret laboratory used to perpetrate the Bre-X gold hoax. They say workers at the facility doctored samples from the mine to back up claims of a 16 billion stg gold find.
-- ROW BREAKS OUT OVER AUCTION OF HALIFAX SHARES

The Association of Private Stockbrokers and Investment Managers is putting pressure on the Halifax building society in an attempt to reorganise the auction of members' shares when it floats next month. Halifax is planning to sell shares to institutional investors on behalf of members in a series of auctions and members will receive an average price paid.
INDEPENDENT ON SUNDAY
-- POLICE RAID INSURANCE AGENT

Police officers from the Serious Fraud Office, the Metropolitan Police and the Belgian judicial police have raided the offices of CRM Insurance Services, the provider of management services for companies based in Brussels. They are investigating a 100 million stg insurance fraud, which hit Lloyd's syndicates, insurers and brokers in the City.
-- BCI CEMENTS UNION DEAL

Blue Circle Industries have agreed a deal with trade unions in its UK cement manufacturing division, which could set a new tone for industrial relations. Under the agreement the four unions at Blue Circle Cement will offer improved flexibility and productivity in return for guaranteed pay rises and job security.
-- CBI DEFIANTLY OPPOSED TO THE SOCIAL CHAPTER

The CBI has announced that it is still opposed to Labour's decision to sign up to the Social Chapter over concerns about the impact it will have on British industry. The CBI claims that legislation cuts across national differences and increases the bureaucratic burden shouldered by companies.
-- GREEN LIGHT FOR P&O

The merger of P&O's cross-Channel business with Stena of Sweden is set to be approved by both Brussels and French competition authorities. EU's competition directorate, DG4, has raised no objections to the 410 million stg merger, which will see P&O take a 60 percent share. The venture will increase its market share of cross-Channel traffic to more than 40 percent.
-- AIRLINES BOOST LINK

United Airlines, Lufthansa, SAS, Thai Airways and Air Canada, one of the world's largest international air alliances, are set to announce closer ties. They will unveil the Star Alliance, which will be adopted as a common brand across the group. Each airline will continue to fly in its own livery but will carry the Star logo.
MAIL ON SUNDAY
-- BAN SPARKS PRICE WAR ON CIGARETTES

The Government's announcement that it will ban tobacco advertising will lead to a price war in the industry. Imperial Tobacco and Gallaher, Britain's leading manufacturers, and American giant Philip Morris has been working on contingency plans.
-- INSURERS FEAR 150 BILLION STG LEGAL ATTACK

The legal battles surrounding damage to health from smoking may lead to a 150 billion stg bill for insurance companies around the world. London insurance brokers are worried that the losses will be larger than the asbestosis and pollution claims that wrecked the Lloyd's market during the Eighties.
-- BA OFFERS TO INVEST OVER AIR ALLIANCE

In return for Government approval of its alliance with American Airlines, British Airways is offering to invest millions of pounds stg in regional services. BA's chief executive, Bob Ayling, has put the offer to John Prescott, the transport secretary.
-- PRIVATE JAILS ON HOLD WITH STRAW

The Government's launch of a review of the Private Finance Initiative will mean that the future of privately-run prisons remains in the balance. Geoffrey Robinson, paymaster-general, said that Home Secretary Jack Straw's dislike of the prisons could jeopardise their inclusion under the PFI.
-- REGIONS IN PLEA FOR A CASH BOOST

John Prescott, the Deputy Prime Minister, is being urged to redraw regional boundaries to channel funds to struggling areas. Chief executive of Tarmac, Sir John Banham, is leading businessmen in Devon and Cornwall who want their own agency to tackle local economic problems because they have been neglected due to the sharing of funds.
